cells.tense: You are passing this along while staying inside it yourself, right now, with your hands on it.
cells.ask: When something in the ritual stops doing what it was for, carry that news to the person who'd want it, and name what you're changing about your own piece of it in the same breath.
cells.core:
You walk into the same room every week and the way you greet people there is a little different each time. You're carrying what the group knows one way while living inside it another, and both are working — nothing has frozen, and nobody's been left holding a version that stopped being true.

The pace is what keeps it alive. You hold the shape of how this goes and also watch when it needs to bend, and that balance gets read as you being calm about change. It isn't calm. It's work you can keep doing. Nothing here has to change for you to keep being right in the middle of it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it alive by letting it move while you hold it.
cells.verb: to carry what a group knows forward into how it lives
cells.place: where energy is aimed at something and held on it

cells.tense: You are already defending a version of this that keeps the people in it from saying what they think.
cells.ask: Next time the way this has been done comes up, let one question land unanswered, and don't fix the person who asked it — let it sit until the next time you're all in the room.
cells.core:
You're walking into rooms already braced. There's a way this is supposed to go, and you can feel the moment before someone colors outside it, so you move early — correcting, steering, keeping the whole thing pointed at a version of how it should land that the people in the room haven't agreed to. The windows are sealed, and you're the one who sealed them.

What you're protecting is real and worth carrying. But it's hard to be in a room where the shape of the evening is already decided. The correctness is costing you the people you're keeping it for, and they're the point.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding this so tight that nobody can move inside it.

cells.tense: You have been working out for yourself how everything holds together, and you have kept that work to yourself.
cells.ask: Find one story, custom or trick from anyone older than you — or anyone far from you — that answers a question you're still solving, and use it, naming who it came from when you do.
cells.core:
When it's going well, you can take a thing apart, see the shape underneath it, and hand that shape to somebody else without the scaffolding you used to find it. You know how the pieces move. That's the thing working, and it's real.

What's running instead is the going-alone part. Nothing you work out gets to lean on what came before it, so every answer gets rebuilt from zero the next time you need it, and the rebuilding eats the momentum you were saving for the actual thing. Somebody already solved part of this — not your version of it, not the way you'd have done it, but the part you're stuck on. It isn't more thinking you need. It's taking one piece you didn't have to build.
cells.sheetLine: You keep reinventing what someone already worked out.

cells.tense: You are already the one people copy, and you describe it as nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Take one thing you decided — a name you use, a way you run a thing, a rule you hold people to — and say out loud where it came from, without softening it into a habit.
cells.core:
Someone in your life is closer to how the group works, is steadier about the rules, and knows what's coming further ahead than you'd say out loud. People take their cue from you and then you file it under just keeping things moving. The steering is happening. Your name is on it, and you're the only one leaving that page blank.

When it's going well, you can feel how much to say and how much to let them find on their own, and from the outside that looks like nothing. What you're doing is the earlier, simpler version of the same act. You're not managing anything. You already are the thing you call nothing in particular.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one they copy. You call it nothing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I had to trim: I wrote that the routine you keep going back to is made of someone else's lines, but the record only says the transmission is running by itself, not where the material came from — so I left the origin unstated. A reader could reasonably say the keeping-up isn't the same as teaching, and the ask survives that: the greeting, holding back, or steel-manning stand whether or not anyone is learning from you. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you've been teaching without meaning to' — it flatters the writer's insight and steps past the person's own account, so the cells use 'asking for something' instead.
